perforated appendix with a 51×31×26 mm collection and surrounding fat stranding
bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy contiguous with soft tissue thickening enveloping the right lower and middle lobe bronchi

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with a collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT.
The patient has a history of prostate cancer in remission and was found to have innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy, suggesting metastatic disease.

The patient was found to have mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, and a thickened, woody sigmoid colon was noted during exploratory laparotomy, suggesting a possible colorectal malignancy.
The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, which are consistent with sepsis, likely due to the perforated appendix.

rationales.F05: Prostate cancer in remission increases the likelihood of metastatic prostate cancer.
rationales.F06: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain is a common symptom of acute appendicitis.
rationales.F10: A perforated appendix is a definitive diagnosis of acute appendicitis.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules could be indicative of metastatic cancer, including prostate or colorectal cancer.
rationales.F12: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy is suggestive of metastatic cancer, including prostate or colorectal cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presented with febrile, hypotensive, and tachycardic symptoms, which are classic signs of sepsis, and the presence of a perforated appendix with peritonism and purulent contamination supports this diagnosis as the immediate cause of sepsis.
